headline: Markets slip as geopolitical tensions and bond uncertainty weigh
deck: Broad equity declines across all three major indices reflect investor caution amid escalating international tensions and shifting interest rate expectations.
body:
Equities finished in the red across the board today, with the Nasdaq leading losses at 1.07% while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones fell 0.74% and 0.67% respectively. The widespread weakness suggests risk-off sentiment as geopolitical headlines continue to dominate headlines, from Iraq troop withdrawals and Iranian rhetoric to Middle East military operations and diplomatic tensions with the UK. Treasury yields remained relatively stable with the 10-year holding near 5.17%, offering little relief to equity investors already grappling with macro uncertainty.

Geopolitical risk premiums appear to be weighing on market sentiment more than economic data today. Multiple developments spanning US military positioning in the Middle East, escalating US-Iran rhetoric, and an unspecified UK airbase incident have created a backdrop of uncertainty that typically pressures risk assets. The tension between diplomatic overtures and hostile statements from Tehran adds another layer of unpredictability for markets already pricing in persistent interest rate levels.

On the earnings and company-specific front, Alaska Airlines' premium cabin overhaul announcement offers a bright spot for investors focused on travel and hospitality sectors navigating a competitive landscape. However, isolated positive news appears insufficient to counter the broader headwinds from geopolitical concerns and investor anxiety around the "new era of interest rates" that bond markets are bracing for according to reporting. Watch for any policy shifts or de-escalation signals that could ease near-term market tension.
